A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLGPO research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original computational experiments on GFP and AAV, including optimization benchmarks, ablations, fitness extrapolation, and appendix sampling analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and additionally reports oracle prediction errors, training-data diversity measurements, and further sampling diagnostics.

M1.justification: The VAE, flow-matching prior, fitness predictors, and manifold-constrained sampling in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 3.3 discusses an alternative maximization-based guidance gradient but explicitly retains the original target-matching procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four GFP/AAV medium and hard optimization tasks. The added oracle diagnostic reuses existing GFP/AAV data; FLIP and ProteinGym are mentioned only as future extensions.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark tables retain GFN-AL, CbAS, AdaLead, BOqei, CoMS, PEX, gg-dWJS, GWG, and GGS. The learned-posterior and without-manifold-constraint comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 adds an oracle assessment using MSE on 512 randomly selected samples from S*. The revised fitness sweep explicitly reports predictor-based fitness. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, 32 ODE steps, and selection of 128 sequences from 512 generated samples remain unchanged; altered heatmap labels alone do not establish an actual search-range change.

E4.justification: V2 adds an oracle accuracy diagnostic and diversity-versus-guidance heatmaps in Figure 6, while revising the fitness sensitivity analysis in Figure 3 and Appendix B.4. Existing manifold, learned-posterior, unconditional-sampling, reconstruction, and ODE-step analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging benchmark results over five seeds and retain the same uncertainty reporting in matched tables and plots. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced; the added MSE is a predictive-error metric.

E6.justification: V2 adds oracle MSEs of 0.012240 for GFP and 0.002758 for AAV, plus training diversities of 14.5/16.3 for GFP medium/hard and 15.9/18.4 for AAV medium/hard. Fitness heatmaps are replaced and diversity heatmaps added. Benchmark and ablation values in v1 Tables 2–5 exactly match v2 Tables 3–6; the changed sweep results do not establish a same-setting performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.3 newly specifies the optional guidance expression (1/2)∇x||gϕ(x)||² alongside the retained target-matching gradient. This is a limited mathematical addition without new proofs or assumptions. The newly numbered Equation 5 merely displays an expression already present inline in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal discussion claims retain the same scope: modular variational optimization in a continuous latent space and state-of-the-art results on the two protein benchmarks. Added supporting diagnostics do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies restriction to GFP/AAV as a limitation and discusses broader benchmarks and structural evaluation. It also adds explanations for GFP/AAV diversity differences, discusses classifier-guidance advantages, and reframes hyperparameter selection around the predicted-fitness/diversity tradeoff.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code availability statement and repository pointer, the predictors' and oracle's 157k-parameter CNN size, and oracle data counts of 56,086 GFP and 44,156 AAV mutants. It clarifies which models use limited data versus S*. These are disclosures about retained components, not documented architecture or training changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dallago et al. on FLIP, Notin et al. on ProteinGym, Stanton et al. on synthetic test functions, and Johnson et al. on computational and experimental evaluation. These support expanded limitations and future directions; the main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 expands selected method and implementation explanations, rewrites Appendix B.4, moves the task definition into Section 4.1, and replaces Appendix A.1 with predictor/oracle documentation. Affiliations are shortened and acknowledgements and an impact statement added. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The task-definition table moves from the appendix to the main text. V1 Figure 5 is replaced by revised fitness heatmaps in v2 Figure 3, and diversity heatmaps are added as Figure 6. Guidance-strength tick labels change from decimal values to 0–35 without an explained mapping. Other figures and table designs are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through code-access information, fuller model/data disclosures, additional diagnostics, and more explicit applicability limits. The gain is limited: the oracle check does not establish held-out reliability, and unexplained guidance-strength scales reduce the revised heatmaps' clarity. The central method and comparative benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
